paper_metadata.title: Inhomogeneous Strains and Dislocation Evolution in Surface-Treated Ni-Base Superalloys

evidence.quote: NI-BASE superalloys show exceptional strength at high temperatures and are often the preferred material when resistance to creep, fatigue, and oxidation is required.
dislocation generation is the dominant mechanism of peak broad- ening in precipitation-hardened Ni-base superalloys
One of the best known examples of this type of superalloy is Inconel 718 which is widely used in jet engine turbine discs in aircraft industry.
mWH3 can model the inhomogeneous strains in Inconel 718 alloys more realistically.

The exceptional creep resistance and high-temperature strength of Ni-base superalloys arise from precipitation hardening imparted by this minor c¢ phase.
The crystal structure of this phase is body-centered tetragonal (BCT) with an ordered arrangement of Ni and Nb/V atoms and it strengthens the alloy primarily by coherency hardening.

conflicts.description: Dislocation density for the 0.12 mmA shot-peened sample differs by an order of magnitude between mWH3 breadth method (4.4(7)e14 m^-2) and CMWP full-profile fitting (54(3)e14 m^-2).

evidence.quote: CMWP fitting procedure predicted a dislocation density value of 54(3) 9 1014 m/C0 2, which is one order of magnitude higher than 4.4(7) 9 1014 m/C0 2, the value calculated from the mWH method.
